pageCache.pageTitle: Curriculum Core Values - St Mark's Primary School
pageCache.text:
Curriculum Core Values
Through consultation with staff, parents and pupils we have developed a curriculum centred around these four key values. Each value is woven through all areas of learning with the aim of developing rounded, outward facing pupils who believe they can make a difference in the world around them and leave our school well equipped with the knowledge, skills and passion to do so.
Our state of mind affects both our mental and physical health. We recognise the importance and benefits of engaging in regular physical activity which develops into lifelong habits. Through our curriculum we will promote children’s collaborative skills and enjoyment of physical activity. Our children will be the best they can be by facing challenges with mental strength, perseverance, resilience and determination.
By developing a deep understanding of historical, cultural, religious and scientific legacies our children will have a strong sense of not only their own identity, but also be able to engage with other identities and cultures. This will enable our children to recognise and challenge discrimination, stereotypes and prejudice.
That everybody has the same basic rights and to be treated with equity is our core belief. Children will understand that fairness may not always mean being treated equally; instead understanding that individuals should receive what they need in order to be successful. Children will understand their roles and responsibilities with a system such a school or wider society. They will be morally principled role models who stand up for their rights and those of others.
Understanding the impact of our actions on our planet, both now and in the future is fundamental to global sustainability. Children will understand the importance of how we share and use the world’s resources fairly and responsibly. Promoting environmentally responsible living while exploring peoples’ dependencies on the environment will highlight how personal choice and the actions we take now can change the future.

pageCache.pageTitle: Teaching British Values - St Mark's Primary School
pageCache.text:
Teaching British Values
Promoting British values at St Mark’s Primary School
The DfE have recently reinforced the need “to create and enforce a clear and rigorous expectation on all schools to promote the fundamental British values of democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty and mutual respect and tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs.”
The government set out its definition of British values in the 2011 Prevent Strategy, and these values have been reiterated by the Prime Minister this year. We reinforce these values in the following ways.
Democracy
Democracy is prevalent within the school. Pupils have the opportunity to take part in the democratic process through voting for their peers to represent classes in our School Parliament, as a Travel Ambassador, or to become a School Captain. Through these systems and the completion of pupil questionnaires we encourage pupils to contribute their views about school. Pupils develop their own rules for their class. Debates and voting are strategies of pupil voice that are regularly used across the curriculum.
The Rule of Law
The importance of Laws is reinforced through teaching around the laws that govern the class, the school and the country. Pupils are taught the reasons behind laws, the responsibilities that we have to live within these laws and the consequences if we break the law. Visits from authorities such as the Police and Fire Service are regular parts of our calendar and help reinforce that laws are in place to protect us and keep us safe. The school operates a whole school code of conduct from which pupils in each class derive a set of classroom rules which are displayed and regularly referred to.
Individual Liberty
Identity is celebrated through our curriculum core values where pupils learn about their rights and responsibilities. They are taught about their rights to be protected from discrimination, to an education and thier freddon to have their own thoughts, opinions and beliefs. Pupils are given clear boundaries in all aspects of school life and are actively encouraged to make choices, knowing that they are in a safe and supportive environment. Pupils are and are given advice on how to exercise these safely, for example through our E-Safety and PSHCE lessons.
Mutual Respect
Respect is a cornerstone of our school ethos and school code of conduct and evident in all we do. Pupils take part in discussions and assemblies related to how we show and earn respect. Displays around the school promote respect for others and this is reiterated through our classroom and learning rules.
Tolerance of those of Different Faiths and Beliefs
Our pupils’ develop their understanding of their place in a culturally diverse society through our broad and balanced curriculum. Pupils celebrate the main religious festivals through assemblies and religious education teaching, including visiting places of worship of the main religions. During lessons, pupils learn about aspects of different faith systems and cultures, tolerance of those with different faiths, beliefs and lifestyles. Members of different faiths or religions are encouraged to share their knowledge to enhance learning within classes and the school. St Mark’s is a safe place where any form of racist or discriminatory language, including homophobic name calling, will be challenged.

pageCache.text:
Vision & Values
St Mark’s Vision and Values
St Mark’s vision is to be a school where children thrive and love to be, where the best staff develop their careers and is the pride of our community.
At St Mark’s Primary School, our CARE values—Community, Achievement, Respect and Empathy— are at the heart of everything we do. They shape our relationships, guide our learning and underpin our ambition for every child.
Community: We value our inclusive school community and embrace the diversity that our children and their families bring. We nurture a sense of belonging, working together to ensure everyone feels welcomed, valued and supported.
Achievement: We strive to challenge and motivate every child to make strong academic progress and become a confident, resilient lifelong learner. Our broad, balanced and accessible curriculum provides stimulating, high-quality learning experiences for all. Teachers and support staff have high expectations of themselves and the children they teach, encouraging everyone to aim high and take pride in their progress.
Respect: We help children develop respect for themselves, others and their environment. We celebrate differences and support children to make positive, thoughtful choices both in school and beyond.
Empathy: We encourage children to understand others’ feelings and perspectives and respond with kindness and compassion. Through caring relationships, we help them recognise how their words and actions affect those around them.
Together, our CARE values help children flourish as learners and contribute positively to their community.

pageCache.pageTitle: Music at St Mark's Primary School
pageCache.text:
Music
Every Child has a Voice
Intent
We recognize the value of music as a fundamental element in children’s cognitive, social, and emotional development and so at St. Mark’s we teach music supported by the Ealing Music Service Scheme, Charanga, which aligns with the National Curriculum for Key Stage 1 and 2. Charanga is an integrated, practical, exploratory and child-led approach to musical learning.
Our curriculum aim is to:
Implementation
Pupils learn through completing two units each term, an overview of which can be found here:
Each unit contains a series of lessons which offer the opportunity to:
Within each unit children listen to and learn a focus song as well as listening to and appraising a range of songs linked to the unit theme. Children are introduced to the interrelated dimensions of music carefully, through a spiral of progressions, shown below.
Lessons are supported with high quality resources and as they progress they are able to achieve each aspect on their Music Passport which can be found on this page, together with Knowledge Organisers for each unit.
Regular assessments, feedback, and performance observations ensure that pupils are making progress, and this is reflected in both their academic outcomes and their emotional and social development through engagement with music.
Peripatetic Lessons and Extracurricular Opportunities: We offer additional instrumental lessons provided by specialist teachers, such as learning the piano, guitar, or violin, as well as a school choir and band to foster a love for performance and collaborative music-making.
Inclusive and Adapted Curriculum: The music curriculum is inclusive and adapted to meet the needs of all learners. We provide additional resources and tailored support for children with SEND to ensure they fully participate in and enjoy music lessons.
Listen and Appraise
Perform/Share
Impact
The impact of our music curriculum is seen through the development of pupils’ skills, knowledge, and attitudes towards music at the end of each stage of their learning. By the time pupils complete Key Stage 2, they will have developed a broad, balanced, and rich experience of music, laying the groundwork for continued study in Key Stage 3 and beyond, as well as fostering personal enjoyment and cultural enrichment.

Joining St Mark’s
Nursery Admissions
St Mark’s Nursery provides a secure, caring and stimulating environment where children are treated as individuals and feel respected, valued and confident.
We have a large nursery, 39 in the morning 8.40am to 11.40am and 26 in the afternoon 12.20pm to 3.20pm. Alternatively we are pleased to be able to offer 30 hours funded or paid for places to our Nursery pupils attending 8.40 – 3.20pm.
We are also pleased to be able to offer Breakfast 7.45 – 8.45am and Afterschool club 3.20 – 6pm on site to Nursery pupils. We work in partnership with Aktiva camps who provide this service. For further information and prices please visit aktivacamps.com.
We admit pupils in the September after their 3rd birthday.
We are accepting applications for places available in our Nursery for September 2027. Please complete the Nursery Application Form and return to the school office.

Before & After School Care
Aktiva Camps
Our Before and After School provider is Ofsted registered Aktiva Camps who provide a Breakfast Club and After-School Club to pupils from Nursery to Year 6 to support our working parents.
Breakfast Club
Aktiva Extended School Clubs run every day during term time from 7.45 am each morning.
A perfect way to start the school day, giving your child a healthy and nutritious breakfast as well as the opportunity to prepare their bodies and minds by participating in a wide range of activities.
An Active Start boosts concentration levels and raises attainment.
Extended School Club
Aktiva After-School Club runs from 3.20pm – 6.00pm.
After a day of structured learning children need to be able to release their energy from being sedentary in their classrooms.
Our after-school care not only provides children with a wide range of activities but offers parents who require childcare up to 6pm peace of mind that they will be kept active and engaged by qualified and experienced staff.
To keep energy levels up all children receive a healthy and nutritious snack.
Contact Aktiva Camps

pageCache.pageTitle: Teaching Pupil Wellbeing at St Mark's Primary School
pageCache.text:
Pupil Wellbeing
Pupil Wellbeing at St Mark’s
At St Mark’s we have a carefully planned approach to supporting our children’s well being. We develop strong relationships based on mutual respect, teaching our children about tolerance and empathy. Through our PSHE curriculum, children develop the skills, knowledge and understanding to become healthy, confident, independent and resilient citizens. Clear routines, and expectations ensure that children understand their rights and responsibilities in school and beyond. We have a trained mental health first aider who champions positive mental health for both staff and pupils, ensuring that well being is planned for, with opportunities for self expression through art, drama and music are available. We are part of the Ealing Schools Counselling Partnership and our staff, children and parents have access to a counsellor and art therapist at school. Lunchtime wellbeing sessions are also available to children who need support.
Our counsellor is Araminta De Clermont and she is on site each week on Wednesday. She can be contacted on 07368-365723 or emailed at araminta@schoolscounsellingpartnership.co.uk
You can call and leave a message or email at anytime and she will respond when she is on site on Wednesday.

Art & Design
Teaching Art at St Mark’s
We aim to inspire every child to see themselves as an artist and to recognise the value of creativity in their lives and futures. We believe that art should be accessible, inclusive and meaningful for all children, regardless of their background, starting point or perceived artistic ability. Through our curriculum, every child is encouraged to develop confidence in their own creative voice and understand that there is a place for them within the world of art.
Our Art curriculum is carefully sequenced to ensure that pupils:
Through a rich range of opportunities, children develop the foundations for future learning in Art. They will:
In Key Stages 1 and 2, pupils build on the creativity, curiosity and practical skills developed in the Early Years. Art and Design is taught through carefully planned units that progressively develop knowledge, skills and artistic understanding.

pageCache.pageTitle: Teaching Computing at St Mark's Primary School
pageCache.text:
Computing
Teaching computing at St Mark’s
A high-quality computing education equips pupils to use computational thinking and creativity to understand and change the world. Computing has deep links with mathematics, science and design and technology, and provides insights into both natural and artificial systems. The core of computing is computer science, in which pupils are taught the principles of information and computation, how digital systems work and how to put this knowledge to use through programming. Building on this knowledge and understanding, pupils are equipped to use information technology to create programs, systems and a range of content. Computing also ensures that pupils become digitally literate – able to use, and express themselves and develop their ideas through, information and communication technology – at a level suitable for the future workplace and as active participants in a digital world. To support the delivery of the computing curriculum the school subscribes to Purple Mash and broadly follows their scheme of work but teachers are able to adjust lessons or use other programs (for example, Scratch) as long as the National Curriculum objectives, as well as those of the school, are being met.
EYFS Implementation
In EYFS, children recognise that a range of technology is used in places such as homes and schools. They select and use technology for particular purposes and are able to complete a simple computer program. They will develop their use of computing vocabulary by using words such as button, switch and application.
KS1 Implementation
In KS1, pupils will develop their understanding of online safety and understand that they should use technology responsibly so that their private information is kept safe. They will learn what to do when something makes them feel uncomfortable and who to talk to about such situations. Pupils will be introduced to algorithms and how they are implemented as programs on digital devices before creating simple programs of their own. Logical reasoning will be used to predict the outcomes of a given set of instructions. Furthermore, pupils will use technology purposefully to create, organise, store, manipulate and retrieve digital content and recognise common uses of information technology beyond school.
KS2 Implementation
In KS2, pupils will understand how to use digital devices and applications in a responsible manner so as not to cause hurt to others or put themselves in danger in the online world. They will design, write and debug programs that accomplish specific goals, including controlling or simulating physical systems whilst learning about coding techniques that enable programmers to write efficient algorithms such as the use of repetition and sequence commands as well as through and the use of variables. There will be opportunities for pupils to use a variety of software (including internet services) on digital devices to design and create content that accomplish given goals, including collecting, analysing, evaluating and presenting data and information. Additionally, children will learn how to use search technologies effectively, appreciating how results are selected and ranked, and be discerning in evaluating digital content (eg fake news). They will also learn the difference between the internet and the worldwide web and understand about the components that enable them to work.

pageCache.pageTitle: Forest School - St Mark's Primary School
pageCache.text:
Forest School
Forest School at St Mark’s
Forest School is a child-centred approach to learning that nurtures the whole child, and at St Mark’s it is a valued and integral part of our curriculum. It provides children with rich opportunities to develop socially, emotionally, physically, spiritually and intellectually through regular outdoor experiences.
We are fortunate to have extensive school grounds that provide inspiring spaces for hands-on learning in nature. These environments help every child grow into a healthy, resilient and independent learner.
During Forest School sessions, children are encouraged to explore, play and take supported risks. They try new experiences, challenge themselves and discover their strengths, building confidence, creativity and resilience along the way. This approach connects closely with the ethos of our OPAL lunchtimes, where children learn through exploration and active play.
By learning to assess, understand and manage risk, pupils develop real-world problem-solving skills, work collaboratively and grow in self-belief – essential qualities that support them both in school and beyond.

pageCache.pageTitle: Teaching French at St Mark's Primary School
pageCache.text:
French
Teaching French at St Mark’s
Children have weekly lessons in French throughout Key Stage 2. In Lower KS2, children acquire basic skills and understanding of French with a strong emphasis placed on developing their Speaking and Listening skills. These will be embedded and further developed in Upper KS2, alongside Reading and Writing, gradually progressing onto more complex language concepts and greater learner autonomy. It is intended that when children leave St.Mark’s Primary School they will have a natural curiosity and confidence to explore other countries, cultures and languages as in a multi-lingual society it is a valuable skill to be able to communicate effectively with others in another language. They will be engaged and prepared to continue language learning at Secondary School. We follow a clear scheme of work covering the National Curriculum and French is taught from Years 3-6 through weekly lessons covering the topics below.

pageCache.pageTitle: Teaching Geography at St Mark's Primary School
pageCache.text:
Geography
Teaching geography at St Mark’s
We want to develop pupils’ love and fascination for the people, places and processes that make up our diverse planet. Our aim is for pupils to gain a rich knowledge and understanding of the world and develop a range of practical skills and knowledge to help them explore the human and physical features around them. From the development of early geographical concepts in the EYFS to explicit geography teaching from Years 1-6, pupils will develop a sound understanding of the different strands of geography and be able to explain the Earth’s key physical and human processes. All children in the school will be able to speak confidently about their geography learning using the correct vocabulary. Pupils will be inquisitive about the world around them and through our curriculum theme, Tomorrow’s World, will develop an understanding of changes to the world’s features over time and their role, as global citizens, in shaping the planet of the future.

pageCache.pageTitle: Teaching History at St Mark's Primary School
pageCache.text:
History
Teaching history at St Mark’s
History at St Marks aims to be ambitious, and motivating. Ambitious through our coverage and thorough teaching of Historical skills, and motivating through engaging activities, trips and visitors that give all students an opportunity to acquire a deep knowledge of and ability to question and understand the past. Pupils in Years 1-6 will be taught History in one lesson each week through half termly units. Our History curriculum has been designed to cover all of the skills, knowledge and understanding as set out in the National Curriculum and to ensure topics and concepts are built on from year to year. Through the History curriculum we aim to inspire pupils to want to know more about the past and to act and think as historians. We want children to develop an enthusiasm and fascination for the world around them and how and why things change over time, including themselves and the world around them. We aim for children to explore their own past and present lives and the lives of their family and over time build a coherent picture of key events, people and places from British and world history. Through our core value, ‘Who are We?’, History at St. Mark’s will develop every students’ cultural capital through exploring the world around them and their own heritage.

Oracy
Oracy at St Mark’s
At St Mark’s, we place oracy at the heart of our curriculum because we believe that the ability to communicate confidently, clearly and respectfully is a vital life skill. Through a structured and inclusive approach to spoken language, we aim to ensure that every child becomes a thoughtful speaker, an active listener and an effective communicator.
At St Mark’s, we see oracy not just as a classroom tool but as a foundation for learning, wellbeing and future success.
